headline: Curiosity doesn't just seek answers—it opens the brain to receive them
universal_truth: The quality of your questions determines the quality of your life
fun_facts: When you're curious about something, your brain releases dopamine—making learning feel like a reward
Curious states improve memory for not just the topic of interest, but everything learned during that time
Children ask about 300 questions per day; adults average around 20
discussion_questions: What are you most curious about right now?
When did you stop asking as many questions—and why?
How could you bring more curiosity to something routine?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Children ask around 300 questions a day. Adults? About 20. Somewhere between childhood and now, most of us stopped being curious. Today, we explore why that matters—and what curiosity does to your brain.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Brain scans reveal something remarkable: when people are curious, their brains light up differently. They don't just learn the answer to their question better—they learn everything better. What makes curiosity such a powerful brain state?

options.text: It releases dopamine which strengthens memory formation
options.response: Yes! Curiosity literally makes your brain better at remembering.
Attention helps, but there's a deeper chemical reason...

q1.title: The Curiosity Cocktail
q1.script: When you're genuinely curious, your brain floods with dopamine—the same chemical involved in anticipation and reward. This doesn't just feel good; it physically enhances your hippocampus's ability to form memories. Curiosity is nature's learning drug.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Curiosity Cocktail"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Spillover Effect
q2.script: Here's what's amazing: the memory boost from curiosity spills over. If you're curious about one topic, you'll remember unrelated information presented at the same time better too. A curious state is like a sponge—everything sticks better.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: 300 to 20
q3.script: Why do adults ask so few questions? Fear of looking stupid. Pressure to seem competent. Busy schedules. But every question not asked is a learning opportunity lost. The most successful people never stop asking 'why?'
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You don't lose curiosity—you suppress it. That wondering child is still inside you, buried under the need to seem like you already know. The bravest question is the simplest: 'Can you explain that?'
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 14—two weeks complete! Tomorrow, we'll explore how your body maintains balance. Until then, ask one question today that you'd normally let slide. See what you learn.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Curiosity Revival - Ask More Questions
growTrack.learning_objective: Reclaim your natural curiosity through deliberate questioning
growTrack.activity: Today, ask at least three genuine questions—at work, at home, or to yourself. Not rhetorical questions. Real ones you want answered. Notice how asking changes how you engage with the world.
